sections.html:
Winterset anchors Madison County, a south-central Iowa county of 16,548 people in 2020. It is the seat of government and the largest town at 5,353. Earlham follows at 1,410, then St. Charles (640), Truro (509), Patterson (176), East Peru (115), Macksburg (97) and Bevington (57, partly in Warren County).

The typical seller owns a small-town house or an acreage, not a subdivision lot, so a buyer judges the parcel and the town together. Weather history counts as well. A low-end EF4 tornado hit just outside Winterset on March 5, 2022. If you have repaired a roof after hail or wind, hold onto the invoices, since lenders and buyers will want to see them.

The Madison County Annex, 201 W. Court Avenue in Winterset, houses both offices you will deal with. One decides what your property is worth, which is the Assessor. The other sends the bill and takes the money, which is the Treasurer.

OfficePhoneWhat to use it for
Assessor(515) 462-4303Values all real property. Weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Mailing address is PO Box 152.
Treasurer515-462-1542Takes property tax payments and handles vehicle titles and licenses. Payment is accepted in person, by mail, or online at iowatreasurers.org.

Values are redone every other year as of January 1. Farm ground is priced on its productive capacity instead of what neighbors paid. Maps and parcel records live on the county's assessor page, which links to the Beacon records site.

Assessment notices arrive around April 1. You then have April 2 through April 30 to file a written protest. If you would rather talk first, the Assessor takes informal review requests from April 2 to April 25.

State law, Iowa Code 441.37, restricts a protest to five grounds:

  • Your value is out of step with comparable property nearby.
  • The figure is above the legal limit.
  • The parcel is exempt, can't be assessed, or sits in the wrong class.
  • Someone made an error in the assessment.
  • Fraud or misconduct occurred, and the protest has to spell it out.

Want to speak at a hearing? Say so in writing when you file. A disaster declaration for the county can move the filing period to May 1 through June 5.

Three county residents make up the Board of Review: a farmer, a real estate broker and a contractor. The conference board names them. The Assessor does not direct how they vote.

Hearings start May 1 and are supposed to wrap up by May 31, unless the Department of Revenue grants more time. You should receive a written ruling that gives reasons. To go further, take the case to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or district court within 20 days of adjournment or May 31, whichever comes later (the Department of Revenue's board of review summary).

In odd-numbered years there is a second window, October 9 through October 31, for owners affected by a state equalization order. The sole argument then is that the order lifts the value above actual value.

sections.h2: Paying property tax and late interest
sections.html:
Iowa lets you settle the year in one payment or two. An unpaid half turns delinquent on October 1 or April 1. From then on, interest is one and one-half percent a month, rounded to the dollar, never under $1, and a partial month is billed as a full month (Iowa Code 445.39).

Walk in to the annex, mail a check to the Treasurer, or pay online. An elderly or disabled owner can apply for that homestead credit through the Treasurer by June 1 of each year (see the Madison County Treasurer site).

If the first half is still unpaid by February 1, a delinquency notice is mailed. A notice that never reaches you does not cancel what you owe.

Delinquent parcels must be offered by the treasurer at a yearly tax sale. It takes place the third Monday in June, barring good cause for a different June date (Iowa Code 446.7). The bid starts at the total of taxes, interest, fees and costs.

Even after the sale, the former owner may redeem. The payoff adds up the sale price, a certificate fee and two percent interest per month starting with the sale month, as set out in Iowa Code 447.1. Those months pile up, so clearing the balance before June is the cheaper route.

sections.h2: What a sale involves for taxes
sections.html:
Whoever records the deed with the county recorder must attach a declaration of value, which a buyer, seller or agent can sign. A copy then goes to the assessor, who files it for three years after the transfer year.

Iowa also charges a transfer tax of 80 cents per $500 of value above the first $500 (Iowa Code 428A.1). Nothing in the statute names the payer, which leaves it to your purchase contract.

The tax attaches to the parcel as a lien, so what is unpaid is normally taken out of your proceeds when you close. The homestead credit follows its own calendar. After a sale before July 1, the buyer files for the credit by July 1. After a sale past July 1, the credit stays put for that year (the Iowa administrative rule).

sections.h2: Before you sell with tax owed
sections.html:
Call the Treasurer at 515-462-1542 and ask for a payoff figure covering tax, interest and fees on each parcel. That number tells you what the sale has to clear.

  • Request the parcel record from the Assessor and look for wrong square footage or class while the April 30 window is open.
  • If a protest is on the table, gather what similar houses sold for in Winterset, Earlham or your township.
  • Report removed or damaged buildings to the Assessor, since owners must report those changes.
  • Before signing, put in writing who covers the transfer tax and the second-half tax.
  • Keep the Treasurer's receipt after closing as proof the parcel was clear.

Someone buying for cash as-is will not ask you to fix the roof or repaint, although liens and back taxes still come out at closing. With the June sale approaching, a cash sale may finish sooner than a listing would, and you avoid showings while it does.

Whichever route you take, bring a short folder to every conversation: the latest tax statement, the Treasurer's payoff figure, the parcel record and any repair invoices. A buyer, a title company or a closing agent will ask for these, and having them ready shortens the whole process by days.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Madison County, Iowa?
faqs.a: Winterset, the largest city too, at 5,353 people in 2020. Both the Assessor and the Treasurer are in the Madison County Annex, 201 W. Court Avenue.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Madison County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 30 and filing opens April 2. Informal review with the Assessor is possible April 2 to April 25. A disaster declaration can push the deadline to June 5.

faqs.q: How often does Madison County revalue property?
faqs.a: Every second year, effective January 1. Owners should tell the Assessor about new construction, remodels, finished basements, decks and any buildings removed or damaged.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the Madison County tax due date?
faqs.a: Interest of one and one-half percent a month begins once the October 1 or April 1 delinquency date passes. Parcels still unpaid may go to the June tax sale.

faqs.q: Who pays Iowa transfer tax when a Madison County house sells?
faqs.a: The rate is 80 cents per $500 above the first $500. The statute does not assign it to either side, so the purchase contract or local custom decides. Your closing agent can tell you which applies.
